lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: noticing without judging

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 4: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice noticing without judging. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: When a body signal shows up, it is easy for a thought about it to turn into a judgment, like thinking a signal shouldn't be happening, instead of a plain observation of what the body is doing.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app
learner-local: a quiet moment to think back over the day

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain whether the neutral noticing statement changed how you felt about the signal itself, and why noticing without judging might be a useful habit even when a signal is uncomfortable.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Judgment-to-noticing conversion: All three rewritten statements are neutral and describe only physical sensations. | Reflection on noticing vs. judging: The reflection names a specific difference between reading the judging version and the noticing version. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner notice one out-loud comment from someone else during the day that sounds like a judgment about a body signal, and privately write how they would rephrase it as a neutral noticing statement, without correcting the other person out loud.

resources.title: noticing without judging coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: When a body signal shows up, it is easy for a thought about it to turn into a judgment, like thinking a signal shouldn't be happening, instead of a plain observation of what the body is doing.
Coach direction: Before you begin noticing today, look at one example of the difference between a judging thought and a noticing statement.
Learner prompt: Which of these is a neutral noticing statement instead of a judgment?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: noticing without judging complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Three separate times today, catch a body signal as it happens. First write down the thought exactly as it first showed up in your head. Then rewrite it as a plain, neutral noticing statement that describes only what your body is doing, with no judging words like 'should,' 'lazy,' or 'bad.'
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote down my first, unedited thought for at least three signals.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I rewrote each one as a neutral statement describing only what my body is doing.
Response 3 (t2-p3): None of my three rewritten statements contain a judging word like 'should,' 'lazy,' 'bad,' or 'good.'
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: noticing without judging minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain whether the neutral noticing statement changed how you felt about the signal itself, and why noticing without judging might be a useful habit even when a signal is uncomfortable.

Success checks: Judgment-to-noticing conversion: All three rewritten statements are neutral and describe only physical sensations. | Reflection on noticing vs. judging: The reflection names a specific difference between reading the judging version and the noticing version.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: noticing without judging supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional noticing without judging condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Judgment-to-noticing conversion: All three rewritten statements are neutral and describe only physical sensations. | Reflection on noticing vs. judging: The reflection names a specific difference between reading the judging version and the noticing version..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.
